per_leaf_remove.behavior: Calls group.commit({ extraProposals: [{ proposalType: defaultProposalTypes.remove, remove: { removed: leafIndex } }] }) — propose+commit in one call. Commit publishes automatically via marmot-ts. Does NOT handle epoch races; throws if epoch advances mid-call.

kind5_delete_pattern.note: Inlined; uses NDK directly (signer.signEvent + NDKEvent.publish), not NdkNetworkAdapter.publish. Targets legacy kind-443 KPs whose private keys are no longer in local IDB. No reusable publishKind5Deletion helper exists — architect can either extract one or replicate inline.
kind5_delete_pattern.usable_via_network_adapter: Yes: unsigned event → signer.signEvent() → client.network.publish(relays, signedEvent). Matches every other marmot-ts publish path.

forget-device is per-leaf, NOT remove-member (memory project_user_action_vocabulary.md). A member only leaves when their last leaf is gone. The spec's design (iterate matching leaves per group) already aligns.

Existing kind-5 deletion in client.tsx:322-335 uses NDK directly. Either replicate or extract a helper through NdkNetworkAdapter — architect picks consistent path.

retrospectives.flag: The three per-client IDB stores (keyPackageStore, groupStateStore, inviteStore) are constructed as local variables inside the init() closure in client.tsx:162-164 and are never exported — forgetSelfDevice therefore cannot reach them to call .clear(), which the spec requires; neither the spec nor any existing seam resolves this, and it will force either exporting these stores to module scope or adding a clearLocalState() method to MarmotClient.

The forgotten-slots IDB store in cleanup.ts:KNOWN_IDB_NAMES is missing by construction (the store does not exist yet), but both the spec and the cleanup helper are in a state where the new feature's IDB store will be silently skipped on the first post-implementation test run unless the implementor knows to add it — a cross-file coupling that will not produce a compile or lint error.
